types.name: AssemblyBodies
types.doc: Groups an assembly's occurrences into rigid bodies, for hierarchy views and simulation links.

fields.name: of
fields.doc: Bodies in the order their first occurrence appears; only tree joints connect occurrences.

types.name: AssemblyBody
types.doc:
A rigid body of an assembly: the occurrences that fixed joints hold together. Moving joints
(revolute, continuous, prismatic) separate bodies, so a body is what actually moves as one piece.

types.name: AssemblyCodec
types.doc: Validation shared by assembly frames and identifiers.

fields.name: containsNul
fields.doc:
Whether text holds a NUL character. Checked by code: a `"\x00"` literal cannot be a HashLink string
constant (and compiled to the text "x00" before haxeon decoded `\x` escapes).

types.name: AssemblyComplianceSpring
types.doc: Series compliance of one parallel spring, in source-coordinate units per effort.

types.name: AssemblyComponentDefinition
types.doc: Connectors belong to a reusable component definition, not an occurrence.

types.name: AssemblyComponentOccurrence
types.doc: An occurrence references shared component data and has a local initial pose.

types.name: AssemblyDefinition
types.doc:
Versioned assembly design data. `assemblies` is a reusable definition table;
an occurrence with `assembly` set names a table entry and exposes only its
declared connectors. Flattening prefixes nested occurrence and joint IDs
with their occurrence path. Runtime coordinates live in AssemblyStateRecord.

types.name: AssemblyDefinitionCodec
types.doc: Versioned transport and validation for reusable assembly definitions and states.

types.name: AssemblyDefinitionFlattener
types.doc: Expands reusable assembly occurrences into the flat mechanical solver schema.

fields.name: flattenState
fields.doc: Maps a saved subassembly root pose to the roots of its flattened members.

fields.name: flattenView
fields.doc:
A read-only flat view. Already-flat definitions are borrowed; nested definitions are expanded.
Call flatten instead when the result will be edited independently of the source.

fields.name: copyActuator
fields.doc: A copy of `actuator` under a new id, on a new joint, with every drive field.

fields.name: copyEncoder
fields.doc: A copy of `encoder` under a new id, on a new joint.

fields.name: copySensor
fields.doc: A copy of `sensor` under the supplied scope prefix.

fields.name: copySwitch
fields.doc: Copy physical switch references into a containing namespace.

fields.name: copyComplianceLaw
fields.doc: Copy every compliance coordinate into its containing joint namespace.

fields.name: copyElasticNetwork
fields.doc: Keep every coordinate and motion-source reference in a network's namespace.

types.name: AssemblyElasticClearance
types.doc: One physical elastic network replaces the scalar springs of its listed motion couplings.

types.name: AssemblyElasticTerm
types.doc: A derived elastic span; displacement coefficients use assembly length per joint unit.

types.name: AssemblyEncoder
types.doc:
An encoder on a joint: it reads the joint's travel in counts. Which joint it sits on says what it
sees. On a motor's own joint it is motor-side and sees the rotor (lost steps, a servo's following
error, but not backlash or belt stretch); on a joint the load moves through a drive it is load-side
and sees where the load is.

types.name: AssemblyExposedConnector
types.doc: A connector exported from a member of an assembly definition.

types.name: AssemblyFrame
types.doc: Rigid frame in the artifact's length unit; quaternion order is x, y, z, w.

types.name: AssemblyFrames
types.doc: Rigid-frame arithmetic shared by CAD generators and project consumers.

fields.name: ROTATION_TOLERANCE
fields.doc:
How far a rotation matrix may be from orthonormal (the largest entry of RᵀR − I) and still be taken as a
rotation: the rounding of entries written to six decimal places. Computed matrices are within 1e-15.

types.name: AssemblyHydraulicDrive
types.doc:
Hydraulic dimensions are assembly length units, phase speeds length units/s and pressure Pa.
Both valve coils off, or both on, select a closed centre; one coil requests extension or return.

types.name: AssemblyJointCoupling
types.doc:
Target coordinate = source coordinate × ratio + offset. A target with several couplings is the sum of
their terms: target = Σ (ratioᵢ × sourceᵢ + offsetᵢ), as a CoreXY motor follows both axes. Each coupling
is one term, with its own efficiency, stiffness, backlash and drag. Every (source, target) pair is
unique and the terms never form a cycle.

types.name: AssemblyJointLimits
types.doc: Missing limits are unbounded. Velocity and effort are optional metadata.

types.name: AssemblyJointStop
types.doc: A mechanical end stop expressed as a contact response.

fields.name: Spherical
fields.doc: Closures only: a shared point.

fields.name: Cylindrical
fields.doc: Closures only: a shared axis line, free to slide and turn along it.

fields.name: Planar
fields.doc: Closures only: the child connector's origin on the parent's plane (normal = axis), normals parallel.

types.name: AssemblyMate
types.doc: A placement relation between two occurrence connectors (see `AssemblyMateKind`).

types.name: AssemblyMateKind
types.doc:
How a mate places its second connector frame B against its first, A, with
a = A's axis and b = B's axis (the mate's `axis`, in each connector frame)
and d = B's origin − A's origin. Mates position parts; joints move them.

fields.name: Coincident
fields.doc: B's origin on A's origin.

fields.name: Coaxial
fields.doc: B's origin on A's axis line, axes parallel.

fields.name: Planar
fields.doc: B's origin on A's plane (normal a), offset by `value` along a; normals parallel.

fields.name: Parallel
fields.doc: Axes parallel (either direction).

fields.name: Perpendicular
fields.doc: Axes perpendicular.

fields.name: Distance
fields.doc: Origins `value` apart (length unit, positive; zero is `Coincident`).

fields.name: Angle
fields.doc: `value` radians between the axes, in [0, π] (0 and π hold the axes aligned or opposed).

fields.name: Lock
fields.doc: B's frame on A's frame.

types.name: AssemblyMotorBrake
types.doc:
A motor driving a joint directly: its usable torque (N m) or force (N), its usable speed in the
joint's units per second, and the inertia of its rotor (kg m²), which turns with the joint.

types.name: AssemblyPneumaticDrive
types.doc: Cylinder dimensions and speed use the assembly length unit; gauge pressure is Pa.

types.name: AssemblyProcessVelocityDrive
types.doc: A CNC speed setpoint in RPM and a signed direction signal drive a continuous joint.

types.name: AssemblySensor
types.doc:
A native discrete sensor mounted to a joint coordinate or a connector face. A `robot_zone`
reports a robot body in any of its `zoneBoxes`: six numbers per box, its centre and half
extents in millimetres, in the connector's frame.

types.name: AssemblyStateRecord
types.doc: A saved configuration, separate from the persistent assembly definition.

types.name: AssemblySubdefinition
types.doc: Reusable nested assembly. Occurrences may reference another entry in the root table.

types.name: AssemblySwitch
types.doc: Geometry-derived switch event on a prismatic joint, in assembly coordinate units.

types.name: BeltCalibration
types.doc:
Effective cord rigidity inferred from a measured single mode, not a belt manufacturer's material test.
Pose values are physical RobotKit joint coordinates in SI, at acquisition. Sources include content hashes.

types.name: BeltCalibrationSet
types.doc: Portable measurement overlay for a source-generated assembly whose parts need not have rebuild recipes.

types.name: ComplianceCoordinate
types.doc:
A parallel sum of springs whose series compliances vary affinely with physical joint coordinates.
A belt span is L(q)/EA; a supported screw is L(q)/EA + 1/K_nut + 1/K_bearing.
Coordinates and compliance use the caller's units, in the coupling's stated coordinate. No samples or callbacks cross the ABI.

types.name: KinematicJoint
types.doc: A persistent kinematic edge or closure. The axis is unit length in the parent connector frame.

fields.name: range
fields.doc:
Tight certified bounds on a finite travel box. Reciprocal positive affine forms are convex.
Maxima are at vertices. Coordinate minimisation supplies a point; its supporting hyperplane supplies a lower bound,
so even early termination never turns a sampled minimum into a claimed worst-case stiffness.

types.name: QuantityAssumption
types.doc: An engineering assumption attached to the quantity that uses it.

types.name: ResonanceMeasurement
types.doc: Results of a validated capture, before model-dependent mass/geometry inference.

types.name: DrawingLine
types.doc: Projected drawing primitives are in millimetres, with +Y upward.

types.name: DrawingProjection
types.doc: Builds vector orthographic views from the portable CAD mesh and its named thread packets.

types.name: DrawingSectionSpec
types.doc: A section keeps the selected half-space of the source part.

types.name: DrawingSvgExporter
types.doc: Physical-size SVG export for an already projected engineering drawing view.

types.name: DrawingViewSpec
types.doc: Orthographic view inputs use the part's model units; direction points toward the viewer.

types.name: Appearance
types.doc: Portable surface finish. Physical/BOM material is a separate property.

types.name: MaterialDef
types.doc: Visual and bulk properties; density is kg/m3, mechanical properties are MPa.

types.name: MaterialKFactorRow
types.doc: ANSI K factor at one nonnegative inner-radius/thickness ratio.

types.name: MaterialLibrary
types.doc: Built-in material definitions shared by generators, the BOM, and the editor.

fields.name: validateSheetProperties
fields.doc: Validate optional structural and development data without assigning defaults.

types.name: MaterialMechanical
types.doc: Strengths and elastic modulus in MPa. Optional for nonstructural materials.

types.name: MaterialRouterCutting
types.doc: Assumed router ranges for stated diameter bands, not supplier recommendations.

types.name: MaterialSheet
types.doc: Sheet development defaults; grain indicates that the authored rolling direction matters.

types.name: MeshMassProperties
types.doc: Integrates a closed, consistently wound triangle mesh as signed tetrahedra.

types.name: SceneArtifact
types.doc: Versioned, producer-independent scene geometry exchange format.

types.name: SceneArtifactArmConfiguration
types.doc: Generic geometric labels, with optional physical arm turn counts.

types.name: SceneArtifactAxisProgram
types.doc: Metre-valued independent-axis waypoints, run as exact-stop moves.

types.name: SceneArtifactController
types.doc:
The controller generates at most `stepTickHz` step edges a second per channel. Driver
microstepping and input-rate limits belong to the machine's actuators; binding combines them.

types.name: SceneArtifactEnclosureGuard
types.doc: Runtime guard policy; door travel and linear speeds are SI, angles radians.

types.name: SceneArtifactFloorPose
types.doc: A pose on the floor: x and y in metres and the heading `yaw` in radians about +Z.

types.name: SceneArtifactGripper
types.doc: Assumed physical limits used to choose and orient a grasp from the blank's planar faces.

types.name: SceneArtifactHeater
types.doc: One heater of a print job; see SceneArtifactPrinting.

types.name: SceneArtifactHobbing
types.doc: Gear/hob lengths in mm, angles radians, process speed m/min.

types.name: SceneArtifactHobbingHandling
types.doc: Authored handling illustration, millimetres; not a deformation/contact model.

types.name: SceneArtifactInspectionCamera
types.doc:
Inspection target is a world-aligned offset from the displayed anchor centre, in metres.
Orientation is steady in world space, so a rotating part never spins the camera.

types.name: SceneArtifactJointTarget
types.doc: Absolute mechanical joint position, in radians or metres.

types.name: SceneArtifactMachining
types.doc:
A machining job the generator made for its own machine, with everything needed to run it (since
version 20). Lengths are metres, whatever the scene's unit.

The machine's `axes` are three prismatic joints whose positions are machine X, Y and Z, and machine
coordinates name where the spindle's gauge line is: the origin of the `spindle` occurrence, whose
+Z runs up the spindle axis. `workOffset` is G54 in machine coordinates. Each tool in `tools` hangs
`length` below the gauge line and has the shape `profile` (a toolpath cutter profile's `encode`),
so the program's G43 H numbers are the tool numbers. `stocks` are the occurrences the tool may cut and
`sacrificial` those it may run into without harm, such as a spoilboard under through holes.
`toolPart` is the occurrence that shows the tool in the spindle, whose shape changes with the tool,
and `loadedTool` the number of the tool in the spindle when the job starts.
`target` names a part of the artifact that no occurrence uses: the finished part, in the stock's
frame, to compare the machined stock with. A looping job starts again when the program ends.
`controller` is the controller the machine's steppers are nominally wired to: the machine's own
limits are the motors' and drives', and the controller's step rate caps them further.

types.name: SceneArtifactMachiningMission
types.doc: A named, single-program machining mission, executed by the CNC player.

types.name: SceneArtifactMachiningSetupJoint
types.doc: Geometric setup condition, in metres for translation and radians for rotation.

types.name: SceneArtifactMissionSignal
types.doc: One digital output command owned by a cell controller.

types.name: SceneArtifactMissionStep
types.doc:
One step of a mission.
- `goTo`: drive the mobile base to `pose`, in the assembly frame on the floor.
- `pick`: take hold of the occurrence `at.occurrence` with the tool, meeting it at its connector
`at.connector`, wherever the part is when the step starts.
- `place`: set what the tool holds down with its base on the connector `at.connector` of
`at.occurrence`, and let go.
- `moveJoints`: move the chain ending at `at` to absolute joint coordinates in radians or metres.
- `signal`: set one digital output on the mission's controller.
- `waitFor`: wait for one digital input on the mission's controller until its simulation-time timeout.
- `moveVia`: move the chain ending at `at` through exact-stop joint or robot-root-frame pose waypoints.
- `weld`: weld the seam `weld` describes with the robot's torch.
- `screw`: pick and drive the named CAD fastening with the robot's screwdriver.
- `findWork`: measure the named work frame from contact probes on saved nominal CAD faces.
- `changeTool`: dock the current tool and select the named physical tool after measured lock feedback.
- `stow`: return the welding arm to its CAD ready posture using its measured joints and live cell clearance.

types.name: SceneArtifactMissionWait
types.doc: A controller input condition with a simulation-time deadline.

types.name: SceneArtifactMissionWaypoint
types.doc: A waypoint is exactly one of a joint target or a robot-root-frame Cartesian pose.

types.name: SceneArtifactMobileBase
types.doc:
The assembly is a differential-drive robot that rolls on the floor. Its root body
is the chassis, driven over the floor plane in the assembly frame: +X forward, +Z up, the origin on
the floor between the wheels' contacts. `leftWheel` and `rightWheel` are its wheel joints (+Y side
first), each turning about its own axle; the simulation reads each one's rolling direction from
its axis. Lengths are metres, speeds m/s and rad/s, accelerations m/s² and rad/s², whatever the
scene's unit. `footprintLength`/`footprintWidth` are the chassis outline, centred on the origin.

A robot that works in a scene of its own names its occurrence subtree as `robot` (an include id:
its occurrences are `robot/...`) and stands at `origin` (x, y and heading on the floor, in the
assembly frame); everything outside the subtree is its world, held where it stands. Without
`robot` the whole assembly is the robot, standing at the assembly origin.

types.name: SceneArtifactPlace
types.doc: A connector of an occurrence in the assembly.

types.name: SceneArtifactPowerUpOffset
types.doc: Physical initial displacement in SI units from the saved pose of a home-monitored joint.

types.name: SceneArtifactPowerUpSideOffset
types.doc: Startup racking in axis SI units, identified by the physical side home switch.

types.name: SceneArtifactPressBrake
types.doc: Runtime bindings are authored semantic ids; geometry supplies each program step.

types.name: SceneArtifactPressBrakeStep
types.doc: Press travel and gauge setup use millimetres; axis planning converts to SI once.

types.name: SceneArtifactPrinting
types.doc:
A print job the generator made for its own printer. Lengths are metres, whatever the scene's unit.

`source` is the program as the printer's G-code (Klipper flavour: relative extrusion, `M104`/`M109`/`M140`/`M190`,
`M106`/`M107`), in machine coordinates: the positions of the three `axes`, prismatic joints whose values are
machine X, Y and Z (the bed's Z grows as the bed goes down, so the nozzle rises relative to it). The machine starts
where the assembly's initial pose puts it, referenced: a leading `G28` is not run, because the virtual device has
no switch inputs for a CoreXY yet. The `extruder` is the joint of the filament drive gear: it turns
`1 / gearRadius` radians per metre of filament, and the hotend melts at most `maxFlow` cubic metres a second.
`pressureAdvance` seconds (0 is off) is how far the extruder runs ahead of the flow it feeds, averaged over
`pressureAdvanceWindow` seconds; `rampLength` is how far along the path its rate ramps. `meltLag` seconds is how long
the melt takes to follow the filament: what flows out of the nozzle is the feed through a lag of that time, which
pressure advance (of the same time) cancels. `controller` is the
controller the steppers are wired to, as in a machining job.

Each heater (the hotend, the bed) is run by the controller: the host sets its target on the analog channel
`target`, the board's PID and watchdog do the rest, and its report is the `tool_heater` sensor `sensor`, in the
board's slot `slot`, mounted on the occurrence `mount`. The numbers are the controller's tuning and the part's
assumed thermal plant. A heater's `fan` is the analog channel (duty 0 to 1) of the part fan that blows on it;
`feedsExtruder` says that pushing filament while it is below `minExtrusionTemperature` is a fault. `deposit`, when
given, is the occurrence that shows what is printed: the simulation lays the material on it as geometry of its own,
in the frame of the occurrence, whose origin is the machine's zero (the bed's front left corner at its surface),
and it rides the bed. `shaping`, when given, names the axes whose motion is input-shaped and with what: the shaper
(`zv`, `mzv` or `ei`) cancels the vibration of a mode at `frequency` hertz and `damping` ratio, and the other joints
are delayed to stay in step (see `InputShaper`).

types.name: SceneArtifactProgram
types.doc: Program dependencies stay outside the bounded geometry metadata section.

types.name: SceneArtifactRobotSensor
types.doc:
A sensor on the assembly's robot, as its part declares it. A `lidar` scans the
horizontal plane of the connector `mount.connector` of the occurrence `mount.occurrence`, `rayCount`
rays round the full circle from the connector's +X axis, seeing out to `maxRange` metres and scanning
`updateRate` times a second. A `force_torque` sensor reports XYZ newtons and XYZ newton-metres at its
named frame. `id` names it in the robot's observations.

types.name: SceneArtifactRobotTool
types.doc:
A tool on the assembly's robot and how it is worked, as its parts' declared
capabilities say: a `suction` tool seals on what touches the occurrence `contact.occurrence` at its
connector `contact.connector` while the digital process channel `channel` is on, and reports the
vacuum it pulls on the sensor `sensor` when it has one. A `gripper` has physical jaws, closes on
the same kind of digital channel, and uses its native joint switch `sensor` as grasp feedback.

A `torch` tool is a MIG/MAG welding torch: `contact` is the connector at its wire tip (the tool point),
`channel` is the digital channel that lights its arc, `sensor` is its `tool_weld` sensor, and `torch`
describes the welder behind it. A `screwdriver` carries its bit, capacities and named tool joints;
its process sensor and tightening observer are supplied by the driving process. Tool data requires
the current scene schema; older versions are rejected.

types.name: SceneArtifactScrewEngagement
types.doc: Mission-level thread-reaction selection, independent of hole-search sensing.

types.name: SceneArtifactScrewEngagementMode
types.doc: Selects whether thread reaction comes from the qualified process model or a physical coupled screw joint.

types.name: SceneArtifactScrewEntrySearch
types.doc:
Commissioning of a force-guided screw entry (`ScrewEntryController`). Axes are the fastening's: u and v span the
hole plane and n advances into the hole; `virtualMass` and `damping` give u, v, n and the rotations about them.
Lengths are metres, speeds m/s, forces N.

types.name: SceneArtifactScrewdriver
types.doc: Tool capacity in Nm and rad/s, travel in mm, spring rate in N/mm. Joint names identify real tool motion.

types.name: SceneArtifactScrewdriverBit
types.doc: Nominal bit identity, portable without a dependency on MachineKit.

types.name: SceneArtifactShaper
types.doc: One axis's input shaper in a print job; see SceneArtifactPrinting.

types.name: SceneArtifactTool
types.doc: One tool of a machining job's tool table; see SceneArtifactMachining.

types.name: SceneArtifactToolChanger
types.doc: Commissioned changer I/O and the CAD interfaces of every interchangeable tool.

types.name: SceneArtifactToolChangerTool
types.doc: One interchangeable physical end effector and its CAD docking interface.

types.name: SceneArtifactTorch
types.doc:
The welder a `torch` robot tool runs on. `wireSpeedChannel` (metres per minute) and `voltageChannel` (volts)
are its analogue setpoints. The weld circuit closes through the occurrences in `groundedWork` (the work
clamp's member and what is welded to it); the arc strikes only against them. `maxCurrentA` is the supply's
rating, `efficiency` the fraction of the mains power it delivers to the arc, `wireDiameterMm` the wire's
diameter and `stickoutMm` the wire's extension past the contact tip. `maxWireSpeedMPerMin` is the feeder's top
wire speed and `depositionEfficiency` the fraction of the melted wire that reaches the weld; the weld steps' recipes
were made for this wire, and the simulated weld deposits with the same figure.

types.name: SceneArtifactTorchPose
types.doc: A pose in the assembly frame: position in metres and an xyzw rotation.

types.name: SceneArtifactWeld
types.doc:
A weld to run and how. What is welded is a result of the CAD, never authored: `path` is the seams as the CAD
found them, run one after the other as one weld (a straight seam is a path of one segment, the four sides of a
tube a path of four), and the rest is what the generator derived from them, so a player needs no CAD to weld
them. Lengths are metres, whatever the scene's unit.
- `path` is the segments in order, each starting where the one before ends. The torch strikes the arc at the
start of the first, keeps it up along the whole path and ends it at the end of the last. Where one segment's
torch angles differ from the next one's, as at the corner of a tube, the torch turns from one to the other
as it passes the joint. All passes share this CAD path and together deposit the requested leg.
- `frame` is the occurrence the path is relative to, the workpiece's reference member: every pose and normal in the
path is in that occurrence's own frame (metres, with its normals turned with it). A player finds the occurrence where it
stands when the step starts and places the path by it, so the weld follows a workpiece that is not where it was
designed. Without a `frame` the path is in the assembly as designed (the form welds took before it existed).
- `metal` is the occurrence that carries the weld metal: the part the bead is shown on as the welder lays it.
- `legSize` is the leg the weldment asks for.
- `passes` give ordered processes, face offsets, weaving and cooling over that path. The generator derives
their deposited areas from the target leg; the measured final leg is checked against that target.

types.name: SceneArtifactWeldFace
types.doc: Physical CAD identity is separate from a seam's display name.

types.name: SceneArtifactWeldPass
types.doc: Ordered passes over the CAD path. Offsets are metres along its two outward face normals.

types.name: SceneArtifactWeldProcess
types.doc:
How a seam is welded: the wire speed (metres per minute) and voltage (volts) of the arc, the travel
speed along the seam (metres per second), and the sequence around it. The torch approaches from `approach`
metres out along the wire, strikes the arc at the start and holds until it is established, dwells
`startDwell` seconds, travels the seam, dwells `craterDwell` seconds at its end to fill the crater, stops the
wire, lets the arc burn back for `burnback` seconds, and retracts.

types.name: SceneArtifactWeldSegment
types.doc:
One primitive of a weld path, the piece of a seam the CAD found. `kind` says what shape it is: only a `line` so far,
straight from `start` to `stop` with the torch holding its orientation; an `arc` for a curved seam would add its
centre and sweep, and be another kind.
- `seam` is its name as the CAD found it (`member:face|member:face`, the two faces the weld metal fills against,
each in the geometry of the occurrence `member`).
- `faces` carry the two CAD member/face identities; consumers never parse `seam`.
- `joint` is how the members meet; only a `fillet` is deposited so far.
- `start` and `stop` are the poses of the wire tip at the two ends: +Z along the wire out of the torch, +X along
the direction of travel as far as it is square to the wire. They carry the work and travel angles.
- `normals` are the two faces' outward unit normals, which say where the weld metal sits (the fillet
fills the corner they leave open).

types.name: SceneArtifactWeldWeave
types.doc: Frequency is spatial, so timing changes never change the authored weave.

types.name: SceneBlowFeed
types.doc: One commissioned tube/receiver path; seconds, bar and millimetres are explicit.

types.name: SceneContactFace
types.doc: Nominal polygonal CAD patches, including fixtures; lengths are metres in the named work frame.

types.name: SceneContactFilter
types.doc: Which contacts an authored assembly hull participates in.

types.name: SceneContactRegistration
types.doc: Strict saved-data boundary; execution and uncertainty policies belong to ProcessKit.

types.name: SceneContactSurface
types.doc: Explicit simulation contact settings; zero numerical fields keep backend defaults.

types.name: SceneContactWork
types.doc: Contact registration after parking. Nominal is assembly_T_work; uncertainty rotates about the chassis origin.

types.name: SceneScrew
types.doc: A freshly derived CAD fastening. All frames use metres; named occurrences own their live poses.

types.name: SceneScrewDefinition
types.doc: Strict saved-data boundary, shared with the live process program. No CAD or process dependency.

fields.name: replacement
fields.doc: A replacement changes only supply identity and pickup; the qualified connection has one owner.

fields.name: validateScene
fields.doc: Validate identity against the actual named thread packet, never another equal bore.

fields.name: decode
fields.doc: Current wire representation only; older scene versions are rejected by SceneArtifact.

types.name: SceneScrewFeeder
types.doc: One commissioned simulated material path; poses are metres in the named nest frame.

types.name: SceneScrewFeeders
types.doc: Strict current-format material paths, with physical sensor and identified-body ownership.

types.name: SceneScrewInvocation
types.doc: Resolve stage identity without duplicating geometry, qualification or replacement supply.

fields.name: validate
fields.doc: All snug passes precede final; every connection and physical supply has exactly one owner.

types.name: SceneWireJson
types.doc: Preserve JSON numbers before haxeon's integer-token parser can truncate them to Int32.

fields.name: integer
fields.doc: Integer values cannot use the reader's annotated-string map-key conversion.

fields.name: integerFields
fields.doc: Field IDs come from the current generated codec rather than a second authored schema.

fields.name: enumArguments
fields.doc: Current enum arguments are the CAD job, the numeric snug slot or the named final reference.

types.name: ScrewDeliveryMode
types.doc: Explicit acquisition arrangement; a tool receiver never supplies a remote pickup pose.

types.name: ScrewEntrySearchBounds
types.doc: What a force-guided screw entry's travel and run bounds must cover. Lengths are metres, speeds m/s.

fields.name: requiredTravelMeters
fields.doc: Largest TCP displacement from the approach pose: the CAD approach plus the entry advance, the registered region, one servo step.

fields.name: spiralLengthMeters
fields.doc: Path length of an Archimedean spiral from its centre out to `radius`, turns `pitch` apart.

fields.name: minimumRunSeconds
fields.doc: The guarded descent over the approach and the entry advance, plus one complete spiral at its path speed.

types.name: ScrewInvocation
types.doc: A connection is qualified once; its final pass refers to the preceding snug job.

fields.name: Required
fields.doc: Single pass whose exhausted NOK stops the controller program before downstream handling.

types.name: ScrewRecovery
types.doc: Reject pose follows its declared fixture, and a replacement is never another guessed nearby body.

types.name: ScrewSimulationSettings
types.doc: Qualified simulation response, independent of the published torque table.

types.name: ScrewSupply
types.doc: A physically distinct supply for one replacement attempt; lengths use scene metres.

types.name: ThreadHand
types.doc: Hand of a thread, independent of the face's orientation.

types.name: ThreadProfile
